title: How Residual-Stream Updates Travel Through Depth: A Pre-Registered Study of Cross-Layer Dynamics in Transformer Factual Recall
description:
Paper, code, frozen pre-registration protocol, figures and run records for How Residual-Stream Updates Travel Through Depth: A Pre-Registered Study of Cross-Layer Dynamics in Transformer Factual Recall (paper v1.0, 6 November 2026; PDF at paper/paper.pdf).

Because transformer components communicate through an additive residual stream, the update a layer writes is the natural unit of cross-layer computation. Two hypotheses about these updates on factual-recall inputs were pre-registered and the frozen protocol was run on Pythia-410m-deduped, with replication on five further models from three families. The updates are predictable across depth (H1), but that predictability is largely architectural; the prediction kernel is not depth-stationary (H2 fails), which points to a first-order, depth-indexed state-space model. That model beats a matched per-layer baseline, lands within ~0.01 R² of a rank-matched cross-layer transcoder at ~6× fewer parameters, and leads below ~1k examples; the pre-registered causal test returns a clean null (recall is a distributed, magnitude-driven code).

Every paper figure regenerates byte-identically from the tracked run tables via scripts/reproduce.sh (no GPU or model download needed).
